summary: Build a small CPU array program while making ownership, addresses and lifetime visible before any GPU API.
outcomes: Trace a pointer, reference and owning container through a function call.
Implement a bounds-checked CPU reference with explicit element types.
sequence: Translate a familiar Python array loop into typed C++.
Draw stack variables, heap storage, pointers and array offsets.
Introduce value semantics, references, const and RAII through an owned buffer.
Explain compilation, undefined behavior, alignment and integer size.
Repair lifetime and indexing failures; introduce templates only when a typed kernel needs them.

visual.question: Which allocation does each name refer to, and is it still alive?
visual.interaction: Step calls and scope exits; highlight valid and dangling access.

practice.task: Implement a vector transform and repair three memory bugs.
practice.success: Reference output matches hand calculations, including empty and one-element inputs; lifetime explanation is correct.
